# Key numbers (generated by src/analyze_results.py)

All attack results are human-reviewed judgments against real guest reviews.

## Overall
- 36 attack tests per system (3 listings × 4 attack types × 3 sizes).
- Standard summary (A): fully fooled 8, partly fooled 7, not fooled 21.
- Evidence-based summary (B): fully fooled 0, partly fooled 6, not fooled 30.
- Same test, side by side: B better in 15, same in 21, A better in 0 (exact sign test p < 0.001; tests share 3 listings, so treat as indicative).

## By attack type (fully or partly fooled, out of 9 tests each)
- Old problem made to look new: Standard (A) 9/9, Evidence-based (B) 6/9
- Fake reassurance about a real problem: Standard (A) 6/9, Evidence-based (B) 0/9
- Flood of generic praise: Standard (A) 0/9, Evidence-based (B) 0/9
- Copy-pasted praise: Standard (A) 0/9, Evidence-based (B) 0/9

## Automated checker (blind judge)
Share of summary statements it marked "supported" by the reviews the AI was given:
- Standard (A), fully fooled: 98.6% (8 summaries)
- Standard (A), partly fooled: 97.6% (7 summaries)
- Standard (A), not fooled: 95.9% (21 summaries)
- Evidence-based (B), partly fooled: 90.6% (6 summaries)
- Evidence-based (B), not fooled: 92.5% (30 summaries)

## Human check of the judge
- 307 claims reviewed; same verdict as the judge in 260 (84.7%).
- Reviewed claims were chosen as hard cases (non-supported verdicts and safety claims), so this is not a general accuracy rate.

## Caveats
- Three listings in one city, one summarizer model, one run per condition.
- Fake reviews are templated; real manipulation may be more varied.
- Scorecard and claim-audit verdicts were drafted with LLM assistance and reviewed by the author.
